description: Team from Douala, Cameroon, working on geospatial data analysis and workflow automation. We are harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS fire detections into one reliable dataset, with justified matching rules and a clear map for fire managers. Join us to build something useful for Central Africa. We are looking for Earth Science, Statistics, Coding or Data Visualization skills.
summary: Cameroon Fire Calendar is a static web app that turns NASA’s two fire-sensor records into one consistent monthly calendar for Cameroon, from 2012 to November 2026. MODIS and VIIRS count fires differently (VIIRS sees about four times more), so their counts cannot be compared directly. The app rescales MODIS to VIIRS year by year, then compares each month with its 2012-2025 median: in seconds, a forest officer, researcher or journalist can see whether the current season is unusual, and where. The latest final month, June 2026, reads 65% above its usual level. The rescaling was validated by a leave-one-year-out test (4.49% average error with one constant factor, 2.48% with Aqua only), and two sister satellites (NOAA-20, NOAA-21) cross-check the main Suomi NPP series at correlations of 0.999 and 0.998.
details:
Problem: NASA's MODIS and VIIRS fire sensors count fires differently. VIIRS has smaller pixels and records about four times more detections, so the two records cannot be compared directly, and fire managers have no single consistent history of Cameroon.

What the project does: a static web app shows one monthly calendar of fire detections for Cameroon, from 2012 to 2 November 2026 for the main series. Suomi NPP (VIIRS) is the reference because it covers the whole period without counting the same fire twice; MODIS is rescaled to it year by year. Each month is compared with its usual level (the median of that calendar month over 2012-2025). A map shows the detections per 0.5 degree cell, a Compare two years view puts two seasons side by side, and the values can be exported as CSV. Months still based on near-real-time data, and the last five months, are hatched and marked provisional. Incomplete months are left empty, not extrapolated.

How it was checked: each year is left out in turn and predicted from the others. A constant factor gives an average error of 4.49%; matching MODIS with Aqua only (same overpass time) gives 2.48%. The 2.48% figure is measured (leave-one-year-out test with Aqua only); the published series still uses each year's own all-MODIS factor. NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 are used only as a cross-check (correlation 0.999 and 0.998 with Suomi NPP), never added to the count.

Limits, stated in the app: detections are not burned area; the main series ends on 2 November 2026; the downloaded MODIS files contain no detection from 30 August to 8 September 2026, and the cause (no fire or missing data) is not yet verified; 2026 uses the 2025 factor (4.693) because its own factor on January-June alone (5.942) is well outside the 2012-2025 range and is not applied.

Data: NASA FIRMS, MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21). The repository holds only aggregated values, with no raw detections and no key.

Full method with formulas and justifications: https://github.com/kahadjie/cameroon-fire-calendar/blob/main/submission/METHODS.md
